findings.reason: an unstated impossibility test makes the guard optional at the will of the party the guard refuses, so the deliverable needs to name the condition that permits a waiver and who states it.
findings.text: "A stated suite-delta waiver is honoured when the primary measurement cannot be made" leaves who declares the measurement impossible, and on what grounds, unstated, and no other section bounds it (the only other use of "waiver" in the plan, plan.html:153, describes the existing waiver as too narrow, not its scope) — so a run's owner can turn any failed or incomplete replay into a passing promotion with a stated waiver, which removes the §17 base measurement the section is repairing rather than widening it

findings.reason: without a rule for an absent revision the endpoint is reachable only for refusals written after the change, which is not the defect the Why names, and the done-when at plan.html:173 never constructs a legacy verdict.
findings.text: "Each promotion verdict records the code revision it was judged under" is stated only as a forward guarantee and the deliverable gives no rule for a verdict with no recorded revision, yet the refusal §20's Why records (a request refused at 16:24 by a service started at 15:13) was written before any revision was stored, and the stored refusal record today carries only phase, settled reason and time (reckon/crew/promotion_requests.py `_settle`) — so the one case the section exists to release stays terminal after the change and its owner still has to ask again

findings.reason: a wrong module named in plan text costs a review round and a worker stop, and deleting the clause loses no endpoint information: every declared record, tolerance and control is already stated in the prose above it.
findings.text: §19 closes "Write paths: reckon/crew/promotion_records.py, reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py and tests/…", and §20 likewise at plan.html:173, so the two new sections state the modules to change rather than the records and figures they deliver, which fixes a guess about the code the worker should have read (the reuse map belongs to the node brief)
